title: The definability of objective becoming in Minkowski spacetime
version: Synthese 103(3), pp. 355-387, 1995 (Kluwer); DOI 10.1007/BF01089733. Read: Springer landing-page abstract (verbatim) and the publisher's free page-one preview PDF covering pp. 355-356 only (sha256 be00fa93...89a4). Pages 357-387, including the Lemma, Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 1 and all proofs, NOT read.
section_locator: p.355 abstract and Sec. 1 Introduction opening; p.356 (RPM premises shared with Stein; worldline-dependent becoming motivation). Theorem/lemma locators (pp.362-365, 371-372) are known only from Savitt's preprint (pa-savitt-2011-cdlp) and are secondary.
relevance: Closest predecessor for RC-2 deliverable (1): a uniqueness/classification theorem for transitive, metrically definable becoming relations in time-oriented Minkowski spacetime, extended to worldline-dependent relations.
assumptions: As read on pp.355-356 only: becoming relation must be transitive and characterizable in terms of time-oriented metrical relations ('time-oriented', 'transitive', 'metrical relations' are each motivated on p.356). Secondary (Savitt): chronological becoming I-(x) subset of B(x); worldline becoming; worldline transitivity; meshing; reflexivity stipulated for convenience; implicit definability from time-oriented metrical relations (plus the worldline for Thm 2).
conclusion: Authors' claim (abstract, verbatim): 'Stein's uniqueness proof can be extended in a natural way to cover this more general kind of becoming, provided one does not enrich standard Minkowski spacetime by privileging certain sets of worldlines over others in an unwarranted manner.' Secondary statement of Thm 1 and Thm 2 (Savitt): only past chronological connectibility, past causal connectibility, or the universal relation.
proof_status: Proofs not read. Theorem statements known only through Savitt (2011 preprint) paraphrase-quotation; publication status: peer-reviewed journal article; correctness not audited here.
open_questions: Exact wording of Lemma (p.364), Theorem 1 (p.365), Theorem 2 (pp.371-72), Corollary 1(B); whether the paper shows by countermodel that each condition is needed (e.g. Peacock 1992 and Muller 1992 relations as violators of worldline transitivity); dimension assumptions; whether null-cone inclusion is assumed or derived.
limits: Paywalled. Routes tried 2026-10-20: doi.org -> link.springer.com (bot challenge for curl; abstract only after cookie redirect; PDF link redirects to paywalled landing page, USD 39.95); OpenAlex (is_oa false, oa_status closed, any_repository_has_fulltext false); Semantic Scholar API (openAccessPdf status CLOSED, abstract elided); Unpaywall not queried (requires a real e-mail; OpenAlex OA status derives from it); PhilPapers/PhilArchive rec CLITRO/CLITDO (Cloudflare 403); Internet Archive Scholar (no hit); JSTOR (bot challenge). No author-repository copy found. Only pp.355-356 legitimately readable. Theorem statements here are SECONDARY (via Savitt) and must not be cited as read.

title: Chronogeometrical Determinism and the Local Present
version: PhilSci-Archive eprint 8481, deposited 2011-02-07, file header 'Draft as of 1 February 2011', 35 pp.; read via Wayback snapshot of https://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/8481/2/CDLP.pdf (id_ capture 2024; sha256 25d5bfd8...6f004) because philsci-archive.pitt.edu returned 'Request Rejected' to direct requests. Later published as Zeta Books 'Time', pp. 143-180, 2020, DOI 10.5840/zeta-time20207 (published version not read; may differ).
section_locator: Sec.1 pp.1-6 (generic RPPM argument; transitivity point p.5); Sec.2 'The Theorems of SCH' pp.6-12 (chronological becoming p.8 with fn10; worldline becoming and quoted CH p.363 p.8-9; worldline transitivity p.9; meshing p.9-10; LEMMA (CH p.364) p.10; THEOREM 1 (CH p.365) p.10; THEOREM 2 (CH pp.371-72) p.11); Sec.3 'A No Go Theorem?' pp.12-14 (Callender's NU and No Go); Secs.4-5 local present P_gamma(a,b) pp.16-24; Sec.6 pp.24-33.
relevance: Only readable source found that quotes/paraphrases Clifton-Hogarth's Lemma, Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 with CH page numbers, and Callender's 'No Go' theorem. Secondary evidence for CH.
assumptions: Savitt's restatement of CH: time-oriented Minkowski spacetime <R4, eta, up>; becoming relation implicitly definable from time-oriented metrical relations; transitive; chronological becoming I-(x) subset B(x); CH stipulate x in I-(x) and x in J-(x) (reflexivity) 'to smooth the proofs' (fn10); worldline becoming; worldline transitivity; meshing.
conclusion: Savitt (p.10) states CH THEOREM 1: definable + transitive + chronological becoming -> 'past chronological connectibility, or ... past causal connectibility, or the universal relation'; THEOREM 2 (p.11): worldline-dependent collection with worldline becoming, worldline transitivity, definability from metric+worldline -> all relations are I-, or all J-, or all universal. Reports Callender's No Go (p.13): definable + transitive + J- inclusion + NU -> universal. Savitt's own proposal: region-relative becoming over local presents P_gamma(a,b) = I+(a) cap I-(b), with tau about 1 s (pp.17-24); he says definability of further worldline-interval structures 'is open' (p.24).
proof_status: No proofs given (Savitt states he omits CH's proofs, p.7). His own region-relative claims are elementary and argued informally.
open_questions: Exact CH wording and whether Savitt's 'trivial changes in notation' (fn9) altered quantifier structure; whether the published 2020 version revises the theorem statements.
limits: Secondary for CH and Callender. 2011 draft, not the 2020 published text. PhilSci direct access blocked; Wayback copy of the author's own deposit used.

title: Conventionality and Reality
version: Foundations of Physics 49(12), pp. 1336-1354, 2019 (published online 2019-09-03); open access CC BY 4.0; publisher PDF read in full (sha256 6f684345...1ef1e18).
section_locator: Sec.3.4-3.5 reality relation R and Eq.(4) aSb => aRb (pp.1341-1343); Sec.4.1 RP argument steps (i)-(v) (pp.1343-1344); Sec.5.1 transitivity objection Eqs.(5)-(6) (pp.1344-1345); Sec.5.2-5.3 conventionality objection, validity vs soundness (p.1345); Sec.6 ontic/epistemic, Fig.7 classification (pp.1346-1349); Sec.7 Weingard-Petkov argument Eq.(7) (pp.1349-1351); Sec.8 (pp.1351-1352); Sec.9 conclusions (p.1352).
relevance: Explicit premise-by-premise reconstruction of the RP and Weingard-Petkov arguments and a decision tree (Fig.7) of which conventionality positions defeat which premises. Informal, no countermodels.
assumptions: RP premises: (i) cSa => cRa; (ii) bSc => bRc; (iii) bRc and cRa => bRa (transitivity of 'is real for'); (iv) not bSa => not bRa; (v) contradiction. WP replaces S by absolute-elsewhere relation A (Eq.7). Reality relation from Peterson-Silberstein uniqueness criterion (reflexive, symmetric, transitive).
conclusion: Author's claim (Sec.9): conventionality impacts RP depending on ontic vs epistemic reading; transitivity of R does not belong to SR's formalism, so 'SR leaves the debate on the dimensionality of the world underdetermined'.
proof_status: Informal philosophical analysis; argument schemata only; no formal semantics, models, or independence proofs.
open_questions: Whether fixed or direction-dependent epsilon really leaves the RP schema valid in all frames was argued by diagram (Figs.8-9) only.
limits: Cites Stein (1968) as 'J. Philos. 67' (ref 44); the volume is 65 (citation slip). Diagrammatic arguments only.

title: The Rietdijk–Putnam–Maxwell Argument
version: PhilArchive record THYTRA (PhilPapers date 2023); untitled-journal review chapter (text refers to 'Chapter 2', 'Chapter 4', and to Google Scholar counts of 2020-02-13); 63 pp. Read via Wayback id_ capture 20241115202307 of https://philpapers.org/archive/THYTRA.pdf (sha256 45ae3afb...3592), because philpapers.org/philarchive.org returned Cloudflare 403 and the HAL copy hal-04437611 returned an HTML challenge.
section_locator: Sec.2 reality relation (pp.6-8); Sec.3 RPM argument (i)-(vi),(C) (pp.8-10); Sec.3.3 block vs physical determinism (pp.12-16); Sec.4 intro mapping objections to premises (p.19); 4.1 conventionality (pp.20-28, Fig.7); 4.4 presentism objection incl. cone-presentism rerun and fn45 (pp.31-35); 4.5 transitivity objection Eqs.(7)-(10) (pp.36-38); 4.6 becoming objection: Stein's five conditions and 'Theorem 1' (p.39), fn51 on CH, Callender's condition 6 and no-go (pp.40-41), Bigaj's openness relation O and inconsistency argument (p.41, Fig.14); 5 conclusion (pp.53-54).
relevance: The most systematic readable premise-by-objection map for RPM: identifies which objection attacks which of premises (i)-(vi) and restates Stein, Callender and Bigaj conditions. Still informal: no countermodel per premise, no independence proofs.
assumptions: RPM premises (i) cSa; (ii) bSc; (iii) cSa => cRa; (iv) bSc => bRc; (v) bRc and cRa => bRa; (vi) not bSa => not bRa. Stein conditions as listed p.39: definable from time-oriented metrical relations; reflexive; transitive; non-universal; J- inclusion.
conclusion: Author's claims: the four RPM readings (reality, truth, determinism, becoming) reduce to one master 'reality argument' (p.18); 'the validity of the Rietdijk-Putnam-Maxwell argument is underdetermined by the formalism of special relativity' (abstract, p.1); p.3: 'A detailed review and critical analysis of the philosophical literature on the RPM argument is presently non-existent'.
proof_status: Review; Stein's Theorem 1 stated without proof and without page locator in Stein 1991. Callender no-go stated as 'it can be shown'. Bigaj inconsistency argued in one paragraph.
open_questions: Thyssen's Callender condition list (1-6 including non-universality 4 and non-uniqueness 6) is jointly unsatisfiable as printed, yet he says the only relation satisfying 1-6 is U; Savitt's statement of the no-go omits non-universality. Thyssen fn51 says with chronological inclusion B 'would reduce to past chronological connectibility', whereas Savitt's CH Thm 1 leaves I-, J- and U. Both discrepancies need the CH/Callender primaries.
limits: Exact publication venue/version unclear (PhilPapers lists 2023; ResearchGate DOI 10.13140/rg.2.2.16674.71365 not verified and not used). Read via archive copy. Statements of Stein/Callender/Bigaj are Thyssen's restatements (secondary).

title: The relativity of indeterminacy
version: arXiv:2101.04134v1 (11 Jan 2021, quant-ph), read as arXiv HTML (LaTeXML) v1; journal version Entropy 23(10), 1326 (2021), DOI 10.3390/e23101326, not read.
section_locator: Sec.I P1/P2 (relativity principle; finiteness of information density); Sec.II.1 TRNG scenario with Fig.1, assumptions 1 'Local reality' and 2 'Present reality', rejection of 2; Sec.II.2 classical correlated randomness; Sec.II.3 quantum case; Sec.III outlook.
relevance: Physicists' explicit two-premise reconstruction of RP for truth-value (in)determinacy, rejecting the 'Present reality' premise; no formal ablation.
assumptions: Truth values of empirical propositions three-valued (true/false/indeterminate); Local reality: 'Any two observers that locally overlap attribute the same truth values to empirical propositions (including the value "indeterminate")'; Present reality: 'Any two distant observers at relative rest attribute the same truth values ... to empirical propositions about present events'.
conclusion: Authors' claim: the RP argument 'fails, in the assumption that truth values are always shared by observers lying on the same plane of simultaneity'; '(in)determinacy is relative'; determinacy 'propagates in space at the maximal signal velocity'.
proof_status: Informal; scenario-based; no theorem, no model.
open_questions: Whether 'Local reality' plus light-cone propagation is consistent with their correlated-randomness picture at the level of a formal model (not attempted in the paper).
limits: Uses 'determinacy' in a truth-value sense; distinct from physical determinism and from ontological eternalism. Published Entropy version unread.

title: Time and Physical Geometry. A Formalization of Putnam’s Proof
version: Logic and Logical Philosophy 29(1), pp. 97-114, 2020 (published online 2019-06-17); CC BY-ND; publisher PDF (sha256 8534b6ce...e838). Polish predecessor Filozofia Nauki 22(1) (2014) 45-57 not read.
section_locator: Sec.2 first proof pp.98-104 (premises (1), I, I*, II, II*, III, (N), (1'), (1'*), III*, (1''*), III'*, lemma (L*), (FP1), (F1), (F1*); contradiction p.104); Sec.3 second proof pp.104-107 ((2), (2''*), III''*, (L'*), (F2), (F2*), (E); transitivity remark p.107); Sec.4 generalization pp.107-109 ((F3), (F3*), III'''*, (L''*), (F2'), (F2'*), 16-step derivation pp.108-109, (F3'*)); Sec.5 standard blocking strategies pp.109-111; Sec.6 non-standard strategy (restricting worldline variables to ether-rest observers) pp.111-112; Sec.7 pp.112.
relevance: Only read source with an explicit symbolic (first-order-style) formalization of Putnam's two proofs and an explicit dispensability claim for one premise.
assumptions: Reality as monadic predicate r; R three-place R(y,x,alpha); premises I*, (1''*) or (2''*), III'*/III''*/III'''*; physical 'facts' (F1*), (F2*), (F2'*), (F3*), (F3'*) asserted as holding in SR (and GR locally) without proof.
conclusion: Verbatim p.107: 'It is worth noting that, for this, the transitivity of R is not necessary, since no assumption here requires this property.' Sec.7: the proofs depend on 'the choice of the standard geometrical interpretation of Relativity'; blocked under the 'dynamical' (Lorentzian ether) interpretation by restricting worldline quantifiers.
proof_status: Derivations are informal-symbolic (one 16-line Hilbert-style sketch with 'trivial intermediate steps omitted'); physical facts F* are not proved; no model theory, no countermodels, no independence proofs, no machine check.
open_questions: Whether the F* facts are each derivable in a stated axiomatization (e.g. Andreka et al. SpecRel); whether restricting worldline variables is equivalent to adding a preferred foliation.
limits: Confirms the defeat-search note (knowledge/defeat-search/rc3-and-clifton-czerniawski.md) at full text: page locators and the p.107 quote are correct. Note: the 'Stein' Czerniawski criticizes is Stein 1968 (ref [19]), not Stein 1991. Blocking checks are informal.

title: Relativistic Quantum Becoming
version: PhilSci-Archive eprint 569 Word file (title page 'Forthcoming in The British Journal for the Philosophy of Science', last saved 2002-02-24), read via Wayback id_ 2024 capture (sha256 634d0b55...bd000), converted with macOS textutil; published BJPS 54(3), pp. 475-500, 2003, DOI 10.1093/bjps/54.3.475 (published text not read).
section_locator: Sec.2 'Classical relativistic becoming' (Stein's six conditions; region extension D_alpha_beta); endnote attached to Sec.2: 'Clifton and Hogarth ([1995]) have disposed of such a notion.' Only Sec.2 and that note were read closely; Secs.3-6 (quantum part) skimmed by keyword.
relevance: Gives a compact six-condition statement of Stein's 1991 characterization (including non-universality and full causal-past inclusion) and the region-relative extension used by Savitt.
assumptions: As listed (verbatim items): 'R is a relation between spacetime points.' 'R is a transitive relation.' 'R is reflexive' 'For any point a, there are points b such that ~Rab.' 'R is definable in terms of the geometry of Minkowski spacetime.' 'Rab holds whenever b is in the causal past of a.'
conclusion: Verbatim: 'Stein showed that the only relation satisfying these criteria is the relation Rxy that holds if and only if either x = y, or y is in the causal past of x.'
open_questions: Whether Myrvold's condition list matches Stein's printed theorem or Stein's surrounding text (the project's audit found the OCR theorem statement lacks two of these).
limits: Preprint, not the published BJPS text; .doc to text conversion dropped list numbering and equation objects.

title: Tense and Indeterminateness
version: PhilSci-Archive eprint 2241 PDF (12 pp., read via Wayback id_ 2024 capture, sha256 2f372cdf...5b70); published Philosophy of Science 67 (Proceedings), pp. S600-S611, 2000, DOI 10.1086/392849 (published text not read).
section_locator: Sec.2 'The Problem With Presentism' pp.1-3 (Ein relation; equivalence-relation requirement; Stein and Clifton-Hogarth); Sec.5 p.6 (Def relation transitive but not symmetric under branching).
relevance: States the 'equivalence relation' (symmetry + transitivity) requirement for a presentist present and reads Stein/CH as showing none is definable; source of the 'CH strengthened Putnam' claim.
assumptions: Presentism requires an invariant equivalence relation definable from Minkowski structure independent of matter distribution.
conclusion: Verbatim p.3: 'Clifton and Hogarth (1995), thinking that they were proving Stein right, went on to prove that no transitive worldline-dependent relation could be defined, given an arbitrary collection of inertial lines. They have strengthened Putnam's point.' Also p.3: Stein's proof 'that Con is the only relation which is transitive, defined in terms of the structure of Minkowski space (Stein 1991). Therefore there is no equivalence relation, proving Putnam's point.'
proof_status: No proofs; relies on Stein and CH.
open_questions: Saunders's paraphrase of CH ('no transitive worldline-dependent relation') conflicts with Savitt's statement of CH Thm 2 (I-, J-, U survive); needs CH primary.
limits: Preprint version; S-page locators of the published version not checked.

title: Special relativity and the future: A defense of the point present
version: PhilSci-Archive eprint 2139 PDF '(Special Relativity and the Future: A Defense of the Point Present)', 38 pp., read via Wayback id_ 2024 capture (sha256 d7939b6b...cb4); published Stud. Hist. Phil. Mod. Phys. 39(1), pp. 82-101, 2008, DOI 10.1016/j.shpsb.2007.06.003 (published text not read).
section_locator: Sec.2 pp.3-5 ('Stein's Theorem' statement p.4); Sec.4 definitions (4.1)-(4.8) pp.15-17; Sec.5 pp.20-27.
relevance: Gives a different premise list for 'Stein's Theorem' and a probabilistic 'relational indeterminacy' definition; shows variation of the theorem's statement in the literature.
assumptions: Verbatim p.4: 'Stein's Theorem: The only reflexive, transitive, and Lorentz invariant relations between world-points in Einstein-Minkowski space-time are the trivial relation, the universal relation, and the relations of past time-like and past causal connection.' Sec.4: probability structure <Omega, A, P>; causal-connection relation caus; Markov screening-off.
conclusion: Author's claim: only the causal past is determinate relative to a point; point-present ('local temporality') is coherent; becoming does not require ontological indeterminacy.
proof_status: Theorem cited without proof. As printed, the 'Stein's Theorem' statement omits the future-directed relations (x = y or y in I+(x); x = y or y in J+(x)), which are reflexive, transitive and invariant under time-orientation-preserving Poincare maps (our elementary observation; not a claim about Stein's printed text).
open_questions: Whether the published 2008 version corrects the theorem statement.
